_meta._note: CNC3D N64 type-code -> mesh mapping. Meshes are OBJs in share/CNC3D/assets/models_table/, named dl_<ROMoffset>.
_meta.method: code-derived. The game keeps ONE unified object-type enum shared by structures, units, aircraft and civilian buildings, and model_index = type_id + 10. Structures read their type_id straight out of a static 64-record array in the CodeOverlay (records 0xAC bytes, name inline, type_id is the byte 5 before the name, first record TMPL at ROM 0x165FDC). Units and aircraft get theirs as the first stack argument (sp+0x10) to their type-class constructors: UnitTypeClass ctor 0x801E92F0 called 16x from ROM 0x18B8A8, AircraftTypeClass ctor 0x801F3C70 called 5x from ROM 0x196058. Verified by rendering every slot from four angles; see work/vmap_struct2.png, work/vmap_units2.png, work/angles.png, work/angles2.png.
negative_results: Spawn_Model at RAM 0x8004BB9C is NOT the unit path and is a dead end for this mapping. Whole-ROM scans: the model table 0x80099998 has exactly 2 code references (Spawn_Model's index at ROM 0x004C7CC and an init loop at 0x0057160); there are exactly 7 jal sites to Spawn_Model, all with constant indices 1,3,4,5,6,7,8,9; and there are ZERO literal function pointers to it, so it is never called indirectly. Spawn_Model only ever places menu/intro models.

The unit ctor argument at sp+0x14 looks like a model index (32-49, with 255 for MHQ/LST/BOAT/A10/C17) but is NOT one: it fails the pixel test, since it puts models at empty slots 34/35/49 and claims A10 has no model when slot 50 is plainly an A-10. It is a cameo/build-list index; 255 means 'not buildable'.

There is no type->modelIndex lookup ARRAY anywhere in the ROM. A whole-ROM scan for an ascending byte run 55..91 (any stride) and 134..140 returns nothing usable. The mapping is arithmetic (id+10), not a table.

CodeOverlay (ROM 0x01643F0-0x01B67D0) contains ZERO data pointers and zero lui/addiu-built addresses into GameModelsGeometry, so the string pools next to 0x1690D0 are not adjacent to any model pointer table.
GAME_STATE_LAYERS-style scene graph in the tail of GameModelsGeometry (class tags CAFEDEAD/DEADCAFE/BEEFED02/FEEB000n at 0x800AC2C0..0x800AC3A0) is a serialized object graph, but it carries no names.
The second table at 0x80099750 (29 entries) is the UI cursor set (arrows, wrench, Nod logo, dollar sign), not turrets.

The earlier tree mapping (T01=113..T18=130, SPLIT2=131) was off by one from T09 onward because it assumed the tree ids were contiguous. Id 111 is skipped, so T09 starts at slot 122 and SPLIT2 shares slot 132 with SPLIT3 rather than owning 131. The visual anchors (rock block, golden crown) could not detect that, since the mis-assigned slots hold look-alike trees.
_meta.segments_note: Nine of these models live in the ScriptModels segment (RAM 0x80122B60-0x801360E0, ROM = RAM - 0x8005BCC0), not GameModelsGeometry: TMPL, FACT, SAM, FTNK, STNK, HTNK, BOAT, TRAN, ORCA. They are exactly the models with moving parts. Earlier passes used 0x80130830 as the end of ScriptModels, which is wrong (that is ReplayMission's RAM base); with the correct bound these nine stop rendering blank.

table_blocks.0-9: menu / intro models. Confirmed independently: these are the ONLY indices Spawn_Model (RAM 0x8004BB9C) is ever called with (constants 1,3,4,5,6,7,8,9 at ROM 0x004ED74-0x004EE54). This is why the unified type enum is offset by +10.
table_blocks.108-112: NULL (game type ids 98-102). Unclaimed: no terrain, structure, unit or civilian type registers these. They are NOT the tree clumps.
table_blocks.113-132: terrain trees, RESOLVED by lookup. TerrainTypeClass registration chain at ROM 0x018CE30: T01..T08 = ids 103-110 (slots 113-120), T09..T18 = ids 112-121 (slots 122-131), SPLIT2 and SPLIT3 BOTH = id 122 (slot 132, the blossom tree). Id 111 / slot 121 is unclaimed. Only 8 distinct tree meshes exist and the ROM's own record array repeats their 8 Gfx pointers with period 8 from slot 113, so T01/T16, T02/T09/T17, T03/T10/T18 etc. share a mesh. That repetition is read out of the ROM, not synthesised by the exporter.
table_blocks.133: NULL (game type id 123). Unclaimed, and it bounds the rock block.
table_blocks.134-140: ROCK1..ROCK7 = ids 124-130, CONFIRMED by the same registration chain. Desert only.
table_blocks.55-91: civilian buildings V01..V37 (type_id 45-81) - CONFIRMED, and the calibration for the +10 offset
table_blocks.92-97: ROAD + the 5 wall types (SBAG/CYCL/BRIK/BARB/WOOD). NOT part of the unified enum: their records store 232-236, which is out of table range, consistent with walls being drawn as terrain overlays.

terrain_lookup.TC01_TC05: registered as real multi-cell terrain (occupy lists of 2,3,4,5,6 cells; strength 600) but with NO model index in ANY theater. The N64 build ships no tree-clump mesh, so there is nothing to draw and they stay fallbacks. This is a property of the ROM, not a gap in the dump.
terrain_lookup.bias: slot = id + 10, the same +10 that already applied to structures, vehicles and civilians. Independently re-confirmed here: the init loop at ROM 0x00571D8 walks 219 16-byte records from RAM 0x80099A38, which is exactly ten records past the 0x80099998 that work/table.json was enumerated from.
terrain_lookup.model_index_fields: three ints at sp+0x38 / sp+0x3C / sp+0x40 = the per-theater model index (desert / temperate / winter), -1 where the type does not exist in that theater. Where more than one is set they always hold the SAME index, so one mesh serves all theaters. ROCK1-7 and T04/T09/T18 are desert-only; T08 and SPLIT3 exist in all three. That matches Tiberian Dawn.
terrain_lookup.source: TerrainTypeClass registration chain, ROM 0x018CE30-0x018DE00, 32 calls to 0x801EAC0C, one per terrain type.
terrain_lookup.string_pool: ROM 0x169668 (CodeOverlay, RAM 0x801C7878): T01..T18, SPLIT2, SPLIT3, TC01..TC05, ROCK1..ROCK7 - 32 names, all 32 materialised by lui/addiu inside the chain, one block each.

APCDOOR.evidence: Code-derived. The APC's draw arm (resident ROM 0x0014BD4 / RAM 0x80013FD4) tests UnitType == 5 -- APC, read off the cartridge's own sixteen UnitTypeClass ctor calls at ROM 0x18B9EC..0x18C8D8 -- calls DoorClass::Door_Stage() at RAM 0x801D3C70 and issues a SECOND model command with model index 193 (ROM 0x0014BEC) before drawing the hull at the same position and yaw. 193 plus the +10 bias is model-table slot 203.
